correctness.rationale: The actual norms have total \(T\bar G\), while the source targets have total \(T\bar G M_\alpha\). The \(L_1\) triangle inequality gives the normalized lower bound \(|1-M_\alpha|\). Two explicit positive normalized allocations attain equality on the two sides of one, and any such allocation is realizable by positive source-normalized task weights when all unweighted gradient norms are positive. Strict Jensen inequalities give the exact heterogeneous-rate phase transition at unit asymmetry. Fresh checker replay confirms the formulas.

value.rationale: GradNorm's powered training-rate target is the method's central mechanism and its asymmetry exponent is its sole principal tuning parameter. The theorem shows that exponentiation silently changes the target vector's total gradient mass except at unit asymmetry, producing a sharp, unavoidable auxiliary-loss floor whenever heterogeneous rates are used with the source's common experimental choices below or above one. The result also supplies the unique common rescaling that preserves the intended relative task priorities while restoring exact mean consistency, making the finding directly useful for analysis and possible algorithm design.
